title: Fresh passport or re-issue: which one should I apply for?
Passport validity, 36-page and 60-page booklets
body:
An ordinary Indian passport comes as a 36-page or a 60-page booklet. The 60-page booklet costs more and suits frequent travellers. Minors are issued only the 36-page booklet.

Validity:
- Adults: generally 10 years from the date of issue.
- Minors under 15: 5 years, or until they turn 18, whichever comes first. Leave the 'Validity Required' column blank in the form.
- Minors aged 15 to 18: choose either a passport valid until age 18 or a full 10-year passport. The fees differ. A 10-year passport for this age group needs Non-ECR proof, or ECR will be printed.
- Short Validity Passport: issued in special cases, for example when the court has allowed travel while a criminal case is pending (normally one year). Its renewal validity is decided case by case.

When to renew: you can apply for re-issue up to 10 years before expiry. Many foreign embassies want at least six months to one year of remaining validity before they issue a visa, so check your destination's rule before you book travel.

For current fees, see the article 'Passport fees'.

title: How to apply online and get your ARN
body:
All passport and PCC applications are made online on www.passportindia.gov.in or through the official Passport Seva mobile app for Android and iOS.

Steps:
1. Register on the portal and confirm your email ID, then log in. The portal asks you to reset your password every 3 months.
2. Select the Regional Passport Office (RPO). You may apply at any PSK or RPO in India, whatever your place of residence. To use a different RPO from the one linked to your login, create a new login ID; you can reuse the same email ID.
3. Open 'Apply for Fresh Passport/Re-issue of Passport' and fill in each step: passport type, applicant details, family details, address, emergency contact, previous passport, other details, then preview.
4. Submit. The portal generates a unique Application Reference Number (ARN). Check every detail first: once submitted, the form cannot be edited, and printed particulars come from what you typed.
5. Click 'Pay and Schedule Appointment', pay online and pick a slot. You will get an SMS with the appointment details.

If you do not visit a PSK within 90 days of submitting the form online, you must submit the application again.

Found a mistake after submitting? Ask the Citizen Service Executive at Counter A in the PSK to correct it during your visit.

Use only the official website and app. The Ministry has warned about look-alike websites that collect data and charge extra for filling forms or booking appointments.

title: Passport fees (36 pages, 60 pages, Tatkaal, minors, PCC)
body:
As of October 2026, passport fees follow the Passports (Amendment) Rules, 2026, which took effect on 1 July 2026. The official fee list in the application instruction booklet shows:

- Fresh or re-issue, 36 pages, 10-year validity: Rs 2,500.
- Fresh or re-issue, 60 pages, 10-year validity: Rs 3,500.
- Minor under 18, 36 pages, 5 years or until 18: Rs 1,750.
- Minors aged 15 to 18 who choose a 10-year passport pay the adult fee.
- Replacement of a lost, damaged or stolen passport: Rs 4,250 (36 pages, 5-year validity), Rs 5,000 (36 pages, 10-year validity), Rs 6,000 (60 pages).
- Change of particulars or ECR deletion: same as fresh (Rs 2,500 for 36 pages, Rs 3,500 for 60 pages, Rs 1,750 for minors).
- Police Clearance Certificate: Rs 750.

Tatkaal: add Rs 2,500 to the application fee. For example, a 36-page Tatkaal passport costs Rs 5,000 and a 60-page one Rs 6,000. Pay the whole Tatkaal amount online when you book.

Rebate: fresh applications get 10% off the basic fee for minors aged 8 or below and for senior citizens. The FAQ defines senior citizens as 60 and above.

Diplomatic and official passports carry no fee. Use the Fee Calculator on the portal to confirm the exact amount for your case before you pay.

title: Online payment: methods, validity, failed or pending payments
body:
You must pay online before you can book an appointment at any PSK or POPSK. Payment goes through the SBI gateway. Accepted methods are credit and debit cards (Visa, MasterCard, RuPay), net banking (SBI and other banks), UPI, SBI wallet and SBI bank challan. You do not need an SBI account. SBI net banking carries no extra charge, while card payments may carry a bank charge that is shown on the payment screen.

Key rules:
- A fee paid against one ARN cannot be moved to another ARN.
- A payment stays valid for one year from the payment date. Once an appointment is booked, the year counts from the first appointment date.
- If you paid twice, the RPO concerned refunds the extra amount.
- If you paid but have no appointment yet, use 'Schedule Appointment'. You can confirm your payment with 'Track Payment Status'.

Money debited but status shows 'Pending': check again on the next working day with 'Track Payment Status' on the Applicant Home screen, then book your appointment.

Money debited but status shows 'Failed': SBI refunds the amount to your bank within seven working days. After that, follow up with your own bank. If the refund still does not arrive, contact the SBI helpdesk at customercare.00691@sbi.co.in or 011-41561114 (10 AM to 5 PM). Give your ARN, transaction ID, amount and transaction date.

title: Booking, rescheduling and cancelling a PSK/POPSK appointment
body:
To get an appointment, pay the fee online and choose a slot at a Passport Seva Kendra (PSK) or Post Office Passport Seva Kendra (POPSK). Tatkaal applicants pick an appointment quota. If no early Tatkaal slot is free they may book under the Normal quota instead, but they still pay the Tatkaal fee and get Tatkaal processing.

Rescheduling limits:
- Normal appointments: the FAQ allows rescheduling or cancelling only two times within a year of the first appointment date.
- Tatkaal appointments: only one reschedule, effective 1 April 2023.
- PCC: only one appointment is allowed within a year of the first appointment date.

Freed slots: slots released by cancellations or reschedules return to the pool every day at the Tatkaal appointment opening time for each Passport Office. Applicants can then book or bring forward an appointment. The portal lists the opening time for each office.

POPSK jurisdiction: if your present address is outside the jurisdiction of the RPO you selected, you cannot book or be processed at a POPSK. Book at a PSK instead.

Walk-ins: only emergency or medical cases and pre-approved categories may visit without an appointment, at the discretion of the PSK in-charge or Passport Officer.

You do not need a printed appointment receipt. The SMS with your appointment details is accepted as proof.

title: Visiting the Passport Seva Kendra: what to carry and expect
body:
Every applicant must attend in person, including infants. Biometrics and a photograph are taken at the PSK or POPSK. No agent, relative or office staff can submit the application for you.

What to carry:
- Original documents plus one set of self-attested photocopies. The originals are checked and returned.
- For children under 4 years: one recent passport-size photo (4.5 x 3.5 cm, white background). Everyone else is photographed at the centre.
- Tatkaal applicants: the signed 'Undertaking for Tatkaal Scheme'.
- A printed application receipt is not needed; the appointment SMS is enough.

PSK working hours: Monday to Friday, 9:30 AM to 4:30 PM. Tokens are issued from 9:30 AM to 4:00 PM, and lunch is 1:30 PM to 2:00 PM.

Inside the centre: an electronic queue system serves applicants first-in, first-out. You can check your details at Counter A and ask for corrections there. Senior citizens get assistance and a special token for faster processing.

Prohibited items: laptops, iPads, cameras, sharp objects, sticks or lathis, arms, and corrosive or explosive substances.

If you are refused a token because a document is missing, you may come back to the same PSK with the complete set, subject to the centre's rules.

Avoid touts. The Government has not authorised any agent to promise urgent appointments or faster delivery. Report such offers to your Regional Passport Office.

title: Tatkaal passport: documents, fee and timelines
body:
Tatkaal is the faster route for eligible applicants. You do not need proof of urgency or a gazetted officer's verification certificate. Police verification takes place after the passport is issued.

Documents: bring the usual proof of address, proof of date of birth and Non-ECR proof (if applicable). In addition:
- Applicants aged 18 or above: any three documents from the list of acceptable documents.
- Applicants under 18: any two from items 1 to 6 of the list.
The list includes Aadhaar (PVC card, full letter or digitally signed e-Aadhaar), PAN card, student photo ID, birth certificate, ration card, previous passport (re-issue only), voter ID, driving licence, bank, Kisan or post office passbook with photo, SC/ST/OBC certificate, arms licence, pension documents, and service photo ID from government, PSU, local body or public limited company.

You also need the signed 'Undertaking for Tatkaal Scheme' (Hindi or English).

Fee: Rs 2,500 on top of the normal application fee, as of October 2026. Pay the full amount online.

Timeline: once the application is granted, the passport is expected to be dispatched on the third working day, not counting the day of submission, without waiting for the police report. The FAQ describes dispatch within 1 to 3 days of the PSK visit.

If required documents are missing, the application is put on hold and is not processed as Tatkaal. Files left on hold beyond 90 days despite a reminder are closed automatically. A Normal application usually cannot be converted to Tatkaal later; you may approach the Passport Office with proof of urgency.

title: Who cannot apply under Tatkaal
body:
The Passport Office has the final say on every Tatkaal application. The following categories are not eligible:

- Any change in name.
- Applicants whose present address is outside the RPO's jurisdiction.
- Minors applying with Annexure C (for example, when the parents are divorced or separated).
- People repatriated from abroad at Government cost, deported to India, or who travelled on an Emergency Certificate.
- People of Naga origin (including minors), including those living outside Nagaland.
- People of Jammu and Kashmir origin, including minors.
- Applicants covered by section 6(2)(e) or 6(2)(f) of the Passports Act (criminal court cases).
- Applicants with an adverse police report, on a watch list, habitual passport losers, or anyone who earlier travelled on a forged passport.

Fresh applications not eligible: citizens by registration or naturalisation, adopted children, a child born out of wedlock with a single parent, children born through surrogacy, and minors with a single parent.

Re-issue applications not eligible: lost or stolen passports; re-issue of a Short Validity Passport; passports damaged beyond recognition; change of sex, appearance or signature; change of date or place of birth; and change of father, mother or spouse name.

A damaged passport can still go through Tatkaal if the passport number and name are readable and the photo is intact. If the parents have an adverse record, a minor may still get a Tatkaal passport with approval of the competent authority.

title: Accepted proof of present address
Accepted proof of date of birth
body:
Any one of the following is accepted as proof of date of birth:

1. A birth certificate issued under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969 by the Registrar of Births and Deaths, municipal corporation or other empowered authority. It should show the child's name, parents' names, date and place of birth, sex, and registration number and date. If the child's name is missing, attach a plain-paper declaration signed by the parents giving the name.
2. A transfer, school-leaving or matriculation certificate from the school last attended or a recognised board.
3. A policy bond from a public life insurance corporation or company showing the holder's date of birth.
4. An extract of the service record (government servants) or the pension payment order (retired government servants), attested by the administration officer of the department.
5. A driving licence issued by the state transport department.
6. A voter ID (EPIC).
7. A PAN card.
8. A declaration from the head of an orphanage or child care home on official letterhead.

Items 4 to 8 count only if they show the complete date of birth. A birth certificate is not compulsory for people born on or after 26 January 1989; any document on the list will do.

To change the date of birth on an existing passport, you must apply for re-issue. The request is examined case by case, more documents may be asked for, and it may be refused.

title: Passport for a child (minor)
body:
Anyone under 18 is a minor for passport purposes. A child needs their own passport, because a child's name can no longer be endorsed in a parent's passport.

Consent and annexures:
- Ideally both parents sign Annexure D. Both parents should attend, or one parent may attend with both parents' passports. The PSK in-charge may still ask for the other parent.
- If one parent lives abroad, the parent in India signs the form and gets the other parent's consent on Annexure D.
- If a parent's consent is not available, the applying parent gives a declaration on Annexure C. Annexure C cases cannot use Tatkaal.

Other rules:
- Validity is 5 years or until 18, whichever comes first. Children aged 15 to 18 may choose a 10-year passport.
- Only the 36-page booklet is issued to minors.
- Children under 4 must bring one passport-size photo (4.5 x 3.5 cm, white background).
- Address proof can be in a parent's name, and parents can attest the documents.
- Police verification is generally not needed when either or both parents hold a valid passport with the spouse name endorsed and Annexure D consent is given. The Passport Office decides the final mode.
- Minors are Non-ECR until 18.
- Fee as of October 2026: Rs 1,750, with a 10% rebate on fresh applications for children aged 8 or below.

title: Police verification: pre, post or none, and how it affects dispatch
body:
Police verification (PV) checks the details you gave in your application. The Passport Office decides which mode applies:

- Pre-PV: verification happens before the passport is issued. This is the usual mode for most fresh applications. Dispatch is expected within three working days after a 'Recommendatory' police report reaches the Passport Office.
- Post-PV: the passport is issued first and police verify afterwards. This applies to all Tatkaal cases and to government employees who submit an NOC (Annexure G). Dispatch is expected on the third working day after submission, without waiting for the police report.
- No PV: for example, a government employee with an Identity Certificate (Annexure A), or many minors whose parents hold valid passports. For a Normal application, dispatch is expected on the third working day.

For most re-issues, either no PV or only post-PV is needed, depending on records. The exceptions are a lost passport, a complete change of name, and a passport that expired more than 3 years ago. Complex cases, such as adoption, single-parent minors, major name changes, or doubtful documents, take about 30 days.

Police verify at the address in your form, even if you applied at a PSK under another office. Give all your addresses from the past year.

If your file shows an 'adverse' report, contact the Passport Office to learn why. Ask for re-verification if needed; the passport is processed once a clear report arrives. If PV has been pending a long time and no passport has come, visit the Passport Office concerned.

title: Government employees and annexures A, G, H, F
body:
Employees of central or state government, PSUs and statutory bodies submit one extra document. This document decides the police verification mode:

- Annexure A, Identity Certificate in original: the passport is issued without police verification.
- Annexure G, No Objection Certificate: the passport is issued on post-police-verification basis.
- Annexure H, Prior Intimation letter: the passport is issued on pre-police-verification basis.

Private-sector employees, including private bank staff, do not need an Identity Certificate.

Dependent family members can also skip police verification if they submit their own Annexure A. A minor dependent's passport is then valid only until age 18. Without it, they follow pre-PV, or post-PV if they apply under Tatkaal with the required documents.

A government employee changing name submits the gazette notification of the change issued in their department and a fresh ID certificate in the new name.

Retired government officials cannot skip police verification. Under Tatkaal, with the required documents, they can get the passport on post-PV basis.

Other common annexures: Annexure C (declaration for a minor when one parent's consent is unavailable), Annexure D (parents' declaration for a minor), Annexure F (affidavit for a passport lost or damaged), and Annexure J (joint declaration in lieu of marriage certificate). Married applicants no longer need a marriage certificate or joint affidavit for a fresh passport. All specimens are on the portal's Annexures page.

title: ECR and Non-ECR (ECNR) status explained
Lost, stolen or damaged passport
Changing name, address, spouse name or other details
Tracking your application and Speed Post delivery
body:
Track your application on the portal with 'Track Application Status', or in the Passport Seva app. You can also call the National Call Centre on 1800-258-1800, where you speak to an executive or enter your file number in the IVRS.

To check status you need your 15-character File Number, issued at the PSK, and your date of birth. Both must match the application. Track Status also accepts your ARN or passport number along with your date of birth.

Typical stages: application received at PSK, police verification initiated or pending, police report received, passport granted, printed, then dispatched.

Delivery:
- India Post delivers passports by Speed Post to the present address in your form. You cannot collect it from the Regional Passport Office.
- The applicant should receive it in person. If you are out, the postman may hand it to a family member after checking ID, or return it to the RPO.
- If the status says 'Dispatched' or 'Delivered' but you have nothing, track the Speed Post article number on India Post's tracking service. Then contact the Speed Post centre, and the Passport Office if the article is lost or returned.
- If the passport is returned undelivered, apply to the RPO for re-dispatch with proof of present address. More proof may be asked for, depending on the postal reason.
- If you receive someone else's passport, surrender it at your Passport Office straight away.

title: Police Clearance Certificate (PCC)
body:
A Police Clearance Certificate (PCC) is often required by foreign governments for immigration, work, residence or family visas. You apply for it online through the Passport Seva portal or app, like a passport.

What to bring: your passport in original, with a self-attested copy of the first two and last two pages. Include the ECR/Non-ECR page, any observation page, and the validity extension page for a short-validity passport. If your address differs from the passport, bring proof of present address.

Particulars must match: your given name, parents' names, gender, date and place of birth must be the same in the PCC form and the passport. If any of these has changed, first re-issue your passport with the new details. A change of address, or adding a spouse name after marriage, is allowed with supporting documents.

Other rules:
- One application covers one country only.
- There is no age limit. Minors can get a PCC if a foreign government asks for one.
- The fee is Rs 750, as of October 2026.
- Only one PCC appointment is allowed within a year of the first appointment date, with no reschedules.
- PCC applications are not accepted at Passport Seva Camps or District Passport Cells.
- Once a clear police report is received, the PCC is dispatched automatically to your address.
- No validity is printed on a PCC. Countries generally treat it as valid for six months.

title: Helpline, grievances and escalation (CPGRAMS)
body:
National Call Centre: 1800-258-1800 (toll free). Executives answer from 8 AM to 10 PM, and the automated IVRS runs 24 hours. The call centre can give your application status (keep your File Number and date of birth ready), locate your nearest PSK or POPSK, and register a grievance. It cannot apply for a passport on your behalf, take a lost-passport report, or accept a reply to a show cause notice. A reply to a show cause notice must be sent in writing by post, or given in person to the officer concerned. If the toll-free line has connectivity problems in J&K or the North-East, the portal lists paid alternative numbers.

Registering a grievance online:
1. Open Feedback and Grievances, then Grievance and Feedback, on www.passportindia.gov.in.
2. Register a new grievance. Quote your file number or passport number, your name and your date of birth.
3. Submit. You get a unique Service Request Number on screen and by email from the helpdesk.

Tracking a grievance: use 'Track Grievance Status' with your date of birth plus the service request number, ARN, file number or passport number. You can also track it in the app or through the call centre. Updates are also sent by email. You can also give feedback at the helpdesk in any PSK.

Escalation: you can also file on CPGRAMS, the Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System. If MEA or the Passport Office has not resolved the grievance within a reasonable time, you may approach the Directorate of Public Grievances, Cabinet Secretariat, at dpg.gov.in.

Fraud alert: use only www.passportindia.gov.in and the official Passport Seva app. Do not pay look-alike websites or touts.
